faq.question: What should a first AI workflow pilot prove?
faq.answer: It should test an agreed operational need against the existing process. Assess output quality, review effort and the full operating cost before deciding whether to expand.

faq.question: Where should people remain involved?
faq.answer: Define who owns the process and which decisions need review or approval. The appropriate controls depend on the task, its risks and the consequences of an error.

faq.question: Does running AI locally guarantee privacy or lower costs?
faq.answer: No. Check the entire data flow, access controls, external connections, hardware and support requirements before comparing a local design with a cloud service.

the-hidden-cost-of-ai-token-usage.reviewType: Company perspective and guidance; no client outcomes claimed.

faq.question: How should we measure the cost of an AI workflow?
faq.answer: Account for model calls, the context supplied and the output generated, using the provider’s actual billing rules. Include review, corrections, infrastructure and support when assessing the complete task.

faq.question: Does using a smaller model guarantee savings?
faq.answer: No. Test its output and the work needed to correct or review it; a cheaper model call is not necessarily a cheaper completed task.

faq.question: What should users be able to see in an AI workflow?
faq.answer: Show the result, relevant supporting information and any decisions or exceptions needing attention. The interface should help people understand and review the work.

faq.question: How do we check whether an interface is useful?
faq.answer: Test it with the people who will use the process. Review their ability to find information, check outputs and recover from errors rather than relying on a demonstration alone.

faq.question: Does a business need to adopt every new AI tool?
faq.answer: No. Choose a real problem and compare a bounded trial with the existing process, including the option of simpler software.
